newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds edge up, spreads mostly even.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds edge up, spreads mostly even.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed prices edged above Friday's closing levels in late-afternoon trade as investors awaited consumer price data on Tuesday.
Yield spreads to comparable Treasuries were unchanged to slightly wider in very light trade, traders said.
"There is no movement in the market, and tomorrow is a relatively big number," said one Ginnie trader, referring to the Consumer Price Index (CPI) slated for release at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.

It appeared investors were waiting to get a clearer picture on whether or not the Federal Reserve bank will lift short-term interest rates at their next two-day monetary policy meeting on July 1-2, the trader said.
"It really doesn't make much sense (to be active) before the CPI data," he added.
At 1545 EDT/1945 GMT, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 3/32 at 100-21/32 bid, yielding 102 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was up 4/32 at 100-19/32 bid, and Freddie Mac issues were up 6/32 at 100-24/32 bid.
The five-year Treasury note was up 4/32 to yield 6.27 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was up 9/32 to yield 6.39 percent.

On average, economists in a Reuters poll forecast consumer prices increased 0.2 percent in May, a tenth higher than April. Excluding volatile food and energy prices, the experts projected CPI rose 0.2 percent in May, slightly lower from the 0.3-percent rise in April.
